🇺🇦 Is Zelensky orchestrating the purge of Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies?

Kiev's Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko this week formally notified NABU Director Semyon Kryvonos that he is a criminal suspect — the legal step that precedes formal charges in Ukraine. In the same breath, Kravchenko called on both Kryvonos and SAP chief Alexander Klymenko to resign, while signaling he'd step down as prosecutor general himself.

According to the Anti-Corruption Action Centre, an NGO aligned with NABU's own network, that timing is no accident. The group reports Kravchenko left Ukraine the same night the suspicion notice was signed — travel that, under Ukraine's wartime exit ban, requires presidential approval. Their claim: the notice against Kryvonos was effectively the price of Kravchenko's exit, personally cleared by Zelensky.

If true, the outline of a plan comes into focus. A simultaneous "clean sweep" — the prosecutor general resigns, NABU and SAP leadership are pushed out — would let Zelensky install a loyalist atop the prosecutor's office, while publicly distancing himself from Kravchenko's move by calling for his resignation too.

The obstacle: neither Kryvonos nor Klymenko shows any sign of resigning voluntarily. Forcing them out would require Zelensky's office to go well beyond a prosecutorial statement — physical detention, a court order, pretrial custody. Whether Zelensky's Office is willing to go that far, or backs down midway, is now the open question. Backing down carries its own cost: it could mean losing control of the security services and his parliamentary majority, while leaving NABU and SAP free to turn their next investigation on Zelensky himself or those closest to him.

➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

Speaking at a weekly press conference in Tehran on Monday, Baqaei said the meeting was intended as an opportunity for Iran and Oman to present their understanding of how to ensure maritime routes and address issues related to the rights and sovereignty of coastal states.
​
Responding to a question from IRNA’s correspondent about the sudden cancellation, Baqaei confirmed that Saudi Arabia had asked that the gathering not be held for the time being.
